risks.note: Customer acquisition runs through Meta and Google. Management states one important event that caused the prior loss-making half-year was a spike in Meta and Google advertising costs, and explicitly says it worries about ad cost ballooning. It claims monitoring mechanisms are now much better so algorithm changes or cost movements can be discovered and tackled early, but the pricing lever itself remains outside the Company's control.
risks.risk: Structural dependence on a small number of advertising platforms whose pricing the Company does not control

risks.note: Management describes the prior H2 FY26 loss as caused almost entirely by advertising costs spiking 2-3x from October 2025, which were not anticipated and took roughly two quarters to fix. Mitigation is stated as strict AI-assisted monitoring of overall costs so unexpected movements are caught early.
risks.risk: High sensitivity of the whole P&L to movement in a single cost metric

risks.note: Management discloses that the Managing Director had to personally take over the advertising function full-time from around February to April 2026 and remains hands-on. He is stated to be bringing in people and AI-driven systems to let the advertising function run with reduced dependency on him, but the dependency is disclosed as a current weakness.
risks.risk: High key-man dependency on the Managing Director

risks.note: Inside sales revenue is disclosed as having crashed from ₹3.5 Cr to ₹2 Cr per month during H2 FY26 because expansion outpaced management bandwidth. A Co-founder was brought in to take over and streamline the function with AI, and is looking to set up a physical team in Indore for more direct monitoring of execution.

As of Q1 2026-27 the sales team is using only approximately 50% of the qualified leads generated by advertising because trainer and sales capacity is the binding constraint. Management frames this as an opportunity, but it is also a structural execution risk: realising growth depends on hiring and training more bootcamp leaders and salespeople.
risks.risk: Delivery-capacity constraint rather than demand constraint

risks.note: The US university plan (Arizona University of Management and Technology Inc.), the microlearning app, the Brihaspati.ai and SkillsafterAI brands, the LawSikho Opportunities job platform and the Justice Scanner legal intelligence tool have all been deferred since the previous year. Management states they are not shelved and will be picked up once the Company achieves predictable net cash, its own internal marker, with all resources and management bandwidth currently directed at regaining profitability.
risks.risk: Continuous deferment of stated initiatives and the resulting execution credibility gap

risks.note: Management flags that the same AI wave cutting the Company's own costs could shrink demand for the entry-level freelance/remote-work outcomes it sells. Stated counters are training students in AI-related skills to raise their hiring potential, and training them to do outreach outside the established remote-work platforms.
risks.risk: AI-driven disruption of the freelance and gig platforms the Company's outcomes depend on

risks.note: The planned US University will require ongoing year-on-year regulatory evaluation once operational, and several Indian certifications benefit from continued recognition under national education policy and bodies like the NSDC — both described as external dependencies outside management's control. Management states this is why the US University initiative will be pursued only when adequate bandwidth exists, and that Indian sales are not dependent on such certifications.
risks.risk: Regulatory and accreditation dependence in India and for the planned US entity

Unlike traditional custom-built stands that are typically designed for one-time use, modular stands are made from prefabricated components that can be assembled, dismantled and reconfigured multiple times based on event requirements. currentContext.expansion: This is an asset-light online education business and the annual report discloses no plants or installed capacity. Management states the build phase is finished, that further significant capital expenditure is not envisaged, and that the Company now expects to derive benefits from the assets already created — reported profitability being depressed by amortisation of capitalised intangible assets, which management expects to continue at similar levels for the next few years before tapering off. Expansion is described as platform and footprint build-out rather than physical capacity: a proprietary ad-serving platform that now launches over a thousand ad funnels per month across Meta and Google, and a proprietary in-house email platform, each replacing paid infrastructure and cutting a specific recurring cost by roughly 80-90%. On the delivery side, management states trainer and sales capacity — not demand or ad cost — is the binding constraint, and that a Co-founder who took over inside sales is looking to set up a physical team in Indore for more direct monitoring of execution. The principal named expansion project, the US university initiative through Arizona University of Management and Technology Inc. (incorporated in Arizona on 24 July 2025, intended to be a step-down subsidiary), is PAUSED, not commissioned: substantial pre-approval groundwork is complete but the initiative was paused in light of a weak quarter until steady net cash generation is achieved, and management describes it as one of the first projects to be restarted once profitability and cash flows stabilise, with Arizona chosen because approval is expected fastest there. A loan of USD 11,067 was disbursed to the Singapore subsidiary Addictive Learning Overseas Pte. Ltd. intended for onward disbursement to the Arizona entity, but was retained by the Singapore entity because the US entity's operations were not initiated during the financial year. Other initiatives — the microlearning app, the Brihaspati.ai and SkillsafterAI brands, the LawSikho Opportunities job platform and the Justice Scanner legal intelligence tool — remain deferred since the previous year and are stated to be not shelved but queued until the Company achieves predictable net cash. On funding, the Company holds ₹7.21 Cr of undeployed IPO proceeds, of which ₹5.21 Cr is sought to be redeployed from unidentified acquisitions and surplus issue expenses towards working capital with shareholder approval, while ₹200 lakhs earmarked for identified acquisition has a proposed revised utilisation timeline up to FY 2027-28.
